title: The Basics
source: Expanded beginner guidance for the current BlockLab controls; original lesson ID retained.

steps.title: Find your way around
steps.check: Find the Shapes button beside the grid.
steps.text: The grid is your building area. Shapes contains new blocks; Objects lists blocks already in your build. This guide stays above the workspace.

steps.title: Place your first Cube
steps.check: A Cube remains on the grid. Properties stays closed.
steps.text: Open Shapes. Press and hold Cube, then drag it sideways onto an empty part of the grid. Release when the preview is in place.

steps.title: Tap to edit
steps.check: The Cube has a blue outline and its name appears in the panel.
steps.text: Tap the Cube and lift your finger without dragging. The properties panel opens. Size, Color, and Move are its three editing tabs.

steps.title: Make it taller
steps.check: The block becomes taller while its bottom stays on the grid.
steps.text: Choose Size. Height controls how tall the block is. Tap the plus button beside Height once; the value changes from 1 to 2.

steps.title: Choose a color
steps.check: Your Cube shows the color you chose.
steps.text: Choose Color, then tap a colored swatch. More colors opens a larger picker. Color changes the selected block, not every block.

steps.title: Move by dragging
steps.check: Moving the block does not reopen properties.
steps.text: Press the Cube and slide it to another place on the grid. Properties closes as dragging starts. Release to place the block; tap it again to edit.

steps.title: Look around your build
steps.check: The view turns while the block stays in the same place.
steps.text: Drag one finger over empty grid space to turn the camera around your blocks. Starting on a block moves that block instead.

steps.title: Zoom and pan
steps.check: You can inspect the block from a comfortable distance.
steps.text: Pinch two fingers together to zoom out; spread them to zoom in. Move two fingers together to pan the view sideways or up and down.

steps.title: Find a block in Objects
steps.check: The same Cube is selected; the build still has one block.
steps.text: Open Objects and tap the block's name. This selects that existing block and opens properties. Objects does not create another block.

steps.title: Undo and redo
steps.check: Undo reverses the last edit; Redo brings it back.
steps.text: Make a small size or color change, then tap Undo in the top toolbar. Open the toolbar's options menu and choose Redo to restore the change.

steps.title: Save your build
steps.check: The toolbar confirms that the build is saved.
steps.text: Tap Save in the top toolbar. Wait until Saving changes to Saved on this device. Save again after making more changes.

steps.title: Finish and reopen later
steps.check: You know how to add, tap, edit, move, and save a block.
steps.text: Choose Mark complete below when you finish practicing. Your saved creation is available in Works. Use Edit build there when you want to continue.

title: Dimensions and shapes
source: Expanded beginner guidance for the current BlockLab controls; original lesson ID retained.

steps.title: Understand the size controls
steps.check: Each control stretches the block in a different direction.
steps.text: Width changes a block across its base. Height changes it from bottom to top. Length changes it from front to back. Change one value at a time.

steps.title: Prepare a Cube
steps.check: Width, Height, and Length are visible.
steps.text: In an empty area, open Shapes and drag in a Cube. Release it, then tap it to open Size. Keep room around it for this exercise.

steps.title: Change the width
steps.check: The Cube is wider, while Height and Length still show 1.
steps.text: Use the plus button or slider to set Width to 3. Width is a size setting for this shape; compare the result with its original value of 1.

steps.title: Change the height
steps.check: The block is now wider and taller.
steps.text: Set Height to 2. The bottom stays in place as the block grows upward. Keep Width at 3 and Length at 1.

steps.title: Make a rectangular block
steps.check: The values are Width 3, Height 2, and Length 2.
steps.text: Set Length to 2. Your starting Cube is now a rectangular block because its width, height, and length are not all equal. Turn the camera to see the depth.

steps.title: Compare before and after
steps.check: Length returns to 1, then back to 2.
steps.text: Tap Undo once to reverse the length change. Then open the top options menu and choose Redo. Notice which dimension changes each time.

steps.title: Try a Cylinder
steps.check: Width changes the round base; Height makes the Cylinder taller.
steps.text: Place a Cylinder apart from the Cube, then tap it. Set Width to 2 and Height to 3. A Cylinder has one width for its round base, so Length is hidden.

steps.title: Try a Triangular Prism
steps.check: Its triangular end and flat faces differ from the Cube.
steps.text: Place a Triangular Prism in a clear area. Tap it and set Base Width to 3, Height to 2, and Length to 2. Look at it from the side.

steps.title: Try a Trapezoid
steps.check: The shape keeps its tapered outline when resized.
steps.text: Place a Trapezoid nearby and tap it. Try Base Width 3, Height 2, and Length 2. Compare its narrower top with the shapes you already placed.

steps.title: Try a Half Cylinder
steps.check: You can describe how this shape differs from a full Cylinder.
steps.text: Place a Half Cylinder in another clear area. Tap it and change Width, Height, and Length one at a time. Look for its curved side and flat cut face.

steps.title: Practice stacking
steps.check: The small Cube rests above the larger Cube without sinking into it.
steps.text: Drag a new small Cube toward the first Cube's flat top. Watch the preview: release when it rests on top. Move it slightly if it remains on the grid.

steps.title: Resize a supporting block
steps.check: The upper Cube stays supported after an accepted resize.
steps.text: Tap the larger Cube underneath and increase Height by 1. Blocks already resting on top move with it. If there is not enough room, the previous size is kept.

steps.title: Use the move handles
steps.check: The handle moves one axis at a time and stops at obstacles or the ground.
steps.text: Tap a block and choose Move. Drag X or Z to move across the grid; drag Y to raise or lower it. Properties stays hidden during the drag; tap the block again to edit.

steps.title: Save your size experiment
steps.check: You have compared all five shapes and practiced resizing, stacking, and moving.
steps.text: Save the build and wait for Saved on this device. Choose Mark complete when you are ready. You can reopen it from Works or continue this lesson later.

title: Build a Simple House
source: Restored from the supplied house lesson; reference images supplied.

steps.text: 1. Create a base using a rectangular block.
2. Create a Triangular Prism for the roof. Match its base width and length to the walls below. Place the flat bottom on top of the base. Sloped faces are not support surfaces.

title: Build a Garden Scene
source: New restoration guidance based on supplied Lesson4 reference images; original full text was absent.

steps.text: Create a green ground block. Build a house, chairs and fences using the reference images.
Add a fountain and flower bushes. Compare spacing, height and colors with the target.

title: Build a City Scene
source: New restoration guidance based on supplied lesson5 reference images; original full text was absent.

steps.text: Create the ground and roads, then add buildings using stacked blocks.
Add a park, benches, bus stop and a car. Keep the scale consistent.

title: Build a Playground Scene
source: Restored from supplied lesson6.dart and images.

steps.text: 1. Create the ground using a Cube. Apply green color for grass.
2. Create a swing using Trapezoids, Cylinders, Half-Cylinders, and Cubes.
3. Add a seesaw using a Cube and Trapezoid.
4. Add benches using Cubes.
5. Create a plant using a Cylinder and Cubes. Use bright colors, keep spacing even and avoid overcrowding.

title: Build a Coffee Shop
source: Restored from supplied lesson7.dart; roof label aligned with the existing Triangular Prism prefab.

steps.text: 1. Create the ground using a Cube. Use gray and green colors.
2. Build the shop using Cubes.
3. Add a roof using a Triangular Prism.
4. Create tables and chairs using Cylinders and Cubes. Keep furniture proportional, use warm colors and align neatly.
